clue.text: The fellow escorting a Spanish lady

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man accompanies a Spanish woman on her evening walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Doña is the Spanish title of respect for a married woman or noblewoman.

clue.text: Planned to study

definitions.meaning: something done on purpose was intended
to ponder carefully is to consider

explanation.surface: Arranged in advance to examine something.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means intentional; as a verb it means to weigh things up carefully.

clue.text: Like music, it's observed

definitions.meaning: music is written down in notes

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that something resembles a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is set down in written notation, and something remarked upon has been noticed: the same past participle covers both.

clue.text: Crawlers inspected possibly about a quarter

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters surround the compass point
possibly suggests the letters of the word before it might be arranged another way

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Creeping creatures were examined, perhaps for around fifteen minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges INSPECTED, and 'about' wraps those letters round E, a compass quarter, not fifteen minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Many-legged arthropods creep along the ground, so they are crawlers.

clue.text: Record — one to preserve for a discriminating person

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one
to cure meat is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A record shows how someone of fine taste keeps things.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of food and drink is choosy about what they consume.

clue.text: Identifying a bird on the heath

definitions.meaning: naming or giving a heading to something
an old name for the meadow pipit, a small moorland bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots something on open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means giving something a name, and is also a dialect name for the meadow pipit.

clue.text: Religious figures taking food with thanks

parts.note: a pie is a kind of food
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Saints accept a meal gratefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: A state of unconsciousness

parts.note: state reads as a condition but is also a country, so a realm visited while asleep

explanation.surface: Someone has passed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary realm of sleep is a country entered only when out cold.

clue.text: Plants in groups

definitions.meaning: puts in the ground, or small bulbs for planting
collections of things that belong together

explanation.surface: Flowers placed in clusters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means puts in place or bulbs ready for planting, and also collections that belong together.

clue.text: Unusual concoction of ale and spice

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rare drink made of beer and spices.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Duty for those who are not quick?

definitions.text: Duty for those who are not quick?

parts.words: Duty for those who are not quick?
parts.note: not quick suggests slow people, but read it as those working after dark: an evening or night stint at work

explanation.surface: A task set aside for the slowcoaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A work period in the evening or night is a spell of duty taken by those who come in after hours.

clue.text: Leave of absence from lunch say

parts.note: ex is Latin for from or out of, as in ex works
to lunch is an example of to eat

explanation.surface: Someone is given time off during their lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is the permission a British boarding school or college gives a pupil to be away for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's formal permission for a pupil to be away briefly is this term.

clue.text: Mark awkward turning for example

parts.note: an awkward situation is a bad one

indicators.note: turning says the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A clumsy bend in the road earns a black mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an identifying emblem or sign, a distinguishing mark.

clue.text: Protesting vociferously when held like a small child

definitions.meaning: people loudly objecting are said to be ...

definitions.text: when held like a small child
definitions.meaning: a baby carried is literally lifted into someone's embrace

explanation.surface: A toddler carried around complains loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for loud outrage also describes, literally, a baby lifted and cradled by an adult.

clue.text: The way issue's taken about single mother, a manual worker

indicators.note: taken about says the street and son go round the next pieces

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a son is issue, offspring
one is single
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A labourer's son is taken around a single mother's road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way' is a street, and 'issue' means offspring, not a problem; 'taken about' makes those two pieces surround the single mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone-cutter or builder works with their hands, a manual tradesman.

clue.text: Convert assets into cash. Get the idea?

definitions.meaning: to sell property for money is to turn it into ready funds
to grasp a point is to understand it

explanation.surface: A financial adviser checks whether the client follows the plan to liquidate holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to sell assets for money and to come to understand something.

clue.text: A qualification men met — and otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters of these words appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Men gathered and agreed a change to the terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges MEN MET AND; the dash is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A change or proviso added to a motion qualifies it.

clue.text: Daring to exasperate a social worker

parts.note: to gall someone is to irritate or exasperate them
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: It takes courage to annoy someone in social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a council employee but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave or spirited deed is a gallant one: daring and chivalrous.

clue.text: Look on an object with abhorrence

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Someone views an item with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense hatred, the same as abhorrence.

clue.text: Where ramblers might well gain support

definitions.text: Where ramblers might well gain support

parts.words: Where ramblers might well gain support
parts.note: ramblers suggests walkers but means rambling roses, climbing plants that lean on a lattice frame

explanation.surface: Hikers find somewhere to be helped along.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice of wood or wire holds up climbing plants such as rambling roses.

clue.text: This is earthshaking!

parts.note: earthshaking seems to mean momentous, but read it literally of tremors in the ground

explanation.surface: A sensational announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes earthquakes, and figuratively anything enormously important.

clue.text: Representative — a good man, and popular

parts.note: ST, saint, is a crossword standard for a good man
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A delegate is described as a decent fellow and well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who acts in another's place is a deputy or representative.

clue.text: He's supposed to send youngsters off

definitions.text: He's supposed to send youngsters off

parts.words: He's supposed to send youngsters off
parts.note: send off suggests dismissal, but means sending children off to sleep, as a figure of folklore does

explanation.surface: A man with a reputation for expelling children.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a figure sprinkles dust in children's eyes to make them fall asleep.

clue.text: New head is set on sticking

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh head is fixed in place by gluing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal for the two words after it, and 'set on' just places the last word after them; 'head' is not a body part here.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the act or state of sticking fast to something.

clue.text: Avoid notice in the evening

indicators.note: in says the notice sits inside the word for evening

parts.note: eve is an old word for evening
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: Keep out of the newspapers at night.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or escape something is to avoid it.

clue.text: A little beast and a thousand women live here

parts.note: a hare is a small animal
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A small creature and a thousand ladies share a home.
explanation.definitionFit: In a traditional Muslim household the separate women's quarters are this.

clue.text: Nonsense written about very large perch

indicators.note: written about says the word for nonsense is put around the next piece

parts.note: rot is nonsense
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Rubbish is published about a huge fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's resting place, a perch, is its roost.

clue.text: Business raised by a masterstroke

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
up means raised

explanation.surface: A company is lifted by a brilliant move.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden brilliant success, a stroke of genius.

clue.text: Some winsome Gallic or Greek character

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A charming French or Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'or', which is only a link word: the definition is 'Greek character'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: So men meet to exchange memorabilia

indicators.note: exchange says the letters of these words swap places into a new order

explanation.surface: Men gather to swap souvenirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepsakes kept to recall events are souvenirs, which together make memorabilia.

clue.text: Put about the smell is getting really bad

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Word gets around that the stench is worsening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something putrescent is in the process of rotting, going off badly.

clue.text: Point-to point organised by school

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
N, north, is another compass point

explanation.surface: A school runs a horse race over the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase in Britain; ETON is the famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English boarding school.
